location.evidence: No state has more than a few of the top or bottom programs, and the outliers show no regional pattern, so location does not explain either end.

prestige.evidence: The best-paying English programs are at far more selective schools than the typical program. Their career offices report that graduates across all majors go into business, consulting, law, media and technology, so the pay follows the school's recruiting reach more than the major.

stepping_stone.evidence: Many English graduates go straight to graduate school. At Cornell, close to a third of English graduates did, and law was their most common field, ahead of English and creative writing.

programs.evidence: Georgetown is a highly selective school in Washington, and its English department says many of its majors go on to jobs in management, media and law.
Yale is one of the most selective universities in the country, and its career office reports that nearly all graduates are working or in graduate school soon after graduating.
Colgate is a highly selective liberal arts college, and its career office lists business, consulting, law and technology among the fields where its graduates go.
Canisius offers a standard English major with no special admission rules or delivery format, and nothing found explains its lower earnings.
Tennessee Tech's English degree has the usual concentrations in literature, creative writing and rhetoric, and nothing found explains its lower earnings.
Marist's figure rests on too few graduates to be reliable.
